site_subset_labels: Connective/soft tissue of head, face and neck
Connective/soft tissue of upper limb and shoulder
Connective/soft tissue of lower limb and hip
rationale: This specific term denotes the extrarenal (soft tissue/visceral) form of rhabdoid tumor; the WHO 5th ed Soft Tissue & Bone volume names 8963/3 'Extra-renal rhabdoid tumour', so by definition it is restricted to soft tissue/peritoneal sites and excludes the kidney (C649), a proper subset of the code's ceiling.
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America - Extrarenal Rhabdoid Tumor (WHO Soft Tissue classification)

rationale: Rhabdoid tumor, NOS is a generic term applying to renal, extrarenal and soft tissue rhabdoid tumors; it occurs across the kidney and soft tissue sites spanning the full ceiling and is not anatomically restricted.

Malignant myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue/skin/bone/viscera occur over a broad anatomic distribution (extremities, trunk, head and neck, bone, breast, viscera, skin), matching essentially the full ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.

Soft tissue myoepithelial carcinoma has a wide anatomic distribution (limbs/limb girdles predominate but trunk, head/neck, bone, breast, viscera and skin all reported), consistent with the broad ceiling; not anatomically restricted.
Infiltrating myoepithelioma is a morphologic descriptor of the same broadly distributed soft tissue/skin/bone/visceral myoepithelial neoplasm family; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Malignant mesenchymoma is a generic mixed-mesenchymal sarcoma descriptor arising across bone and soft tissue sites; it is not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Generic multi-site mixed mesenchymal sarcoma descriptor occurring across bone and soft tissue; not anatomically restricted.

Phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor arises in BOTH bone (~53%) and soft tissue (~45%) across the body (extremities, appendicular/axial skeleton, head and neck), spanning both the bone and soft tissue portions of the ceiling; it is not confined to a proper subset.

A histologic-grade variant of synovial sarcoma, which arises at a wide range of sites (extremities, trunk, head/neck, lung, mediastinum, kidney); the subtype is not anatomically restricted relative to the code ceiling.
Synovial sarcoma, NOS occurs across all validated deep soft tissue and visceral sites; generic descriptor, not restricted to a proper subset.
Poorly differentiated is a histologic descriptor of synovial sarcoma; the entity spans the full ceiling of sites and the subtype is not anatomically restricted.
Synovioma, NOS is a synonym for synovial sarcoma, which occurs across the full ceiling of soft tissue and visceral sites; not restricted.
Malignant synovioma is a synonym for synovial sarcoma with the same broad site distribution; not anatomically restricted.
Monophasic is a histologic subtype of synovial sarcoma; it occurs across the full range of synovial sarcoma sites and is not anatomically restricted.
Histologic subtype descriptor of synovial sarcoma with the same broad anatomic distribution; not restricted to a proper subset.
A histologic pattern descriptor of monophasic synovial sarcoma; not anatomically restricted relative to the code ceiling.
Histologic pattern descriptor of monophasic synovial sarcoma; occurs across the full ceiling of sites, not anatomically restricted.
Spindle cell (monophasic) morphologic descriptor of synovial sarcoma; not restricted to a proper subset of sites.
Biphasic is a histologic subtype of synovial sarcoma; it occurs across the full range of synovial sarcoma sites and is not anatomically restricted.
Histologic subtype descriptor of synovial sarcoma with the same broad anatomic distribution; not restricted to a proper subset.

This is a cutaneous (dermal/skin) entity restricted to the skin, but skin (C44) is not among this code's ceiling_codes (which are retroperitoneum/peritoneum/connective-soft tissue C48-C49); the restriction cannot be expressed as a valid subset of the provided ceiling, so classification within the ceiling is indeterminate.
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America - Clear Cell Sarcoma of Soft Tissue

term: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
rationale: The defining entity for this code; it occurs across deep soft tissue sites of the body (extremities predominate but trunk, head/neck and retroperitoneum are reported), spanning the connective/soft tissue ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.

term: Clear cell sarcoma of tendons and aponeuroses
rationale: Synonym for clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue; although it favors distal extremity tendons/aponeuroses, cases across trunk, head/neck, retroperitoneum and other soft tissue sites are documented, so it is not confined to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Generic term for clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue occurring across soft tissue sites; not anatomically restricted.

A rare dermis/skin-localized variant restricted to the skin; skin (C44) is not among this code's ceiling_codes (retroperitoneum/peritoneum/connective-soft tissue), so the restriction cannot be expressed as a valid subset of the provided ceiling.
source_name: Cureus - Clear-Cell Sarcoma With an Unusual Presentation (dermal localization)

term: Gastrointestinal clear cell sarcoma / malignant gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumor
rationale: This GI-tract entity (GNET/CCSLGT) arises within the wall of the gastrointestinal tract (most often small intestine, stomach, colon); however GI-tract C-codes are not present in this code's ceiling_codes (retroperitoneum/peritoneum/connective-soft tissue C48-C49), so the restriction cannot be expressed as a valid subset of the provided ceiling.
source_name: Am J Surg Pathol - Malignant Gastrointestinal Neuroectodermal Tumor

rationale: MGNET/GNET arises exclusively within the wall of the gastrointestinal tract (predominantly small intestine); however GI-tract C-codes are not present in this code's ceiling_codes (retroperitoneum/peritoneum/connective-soft tissue), so a valid ceiling subset cannot be constructed.
source_name: Oncology Letters - Primary malignant gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumor

rationale: Synonym for clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue; occurs across deep soft tissue sites of the body and is not confined to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Synonym for clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue with the same broad soft tissue distribution; not anatomically restricted.

Mesothelioma in situ was introduced in the WHO Thoracic volume primarily as a preinvasive pleural lesion, but peritoneal in-situ mesothelioma is increasingly recognized; the evidence does not cleanly restrict it to a single proper subset of the pleura/pericardium/peritoneum ceiling.
source_name: Pulmonary Pathology Society - Mesothelioma in situ (WHO Thoracic Tumors)

rationale: Desmoplastic mesothelioma is a sarcomatoid subtype occurring predominantly in the pleura but with documented peritoneal (and rare pericardial) cases; it is not confined to a single proper subset within the serosal-cavity ceiling.
Fibrous (sarcomatoid/spindled) mesothelioma occurs across pleural and peritoneal serosal sites; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
Malignant fibrous (sarcomatoid) mesothelioma occurs in both pleura and peritoneum; not anatomically restricted within the serosal-cavity ceiling.
Sarcomatoid mesothelioma is predominantly pleural (~98%) but arises in the peritoneum as well; it spans multiple serosal sites of the ceiling and is not confined to a single proper subset.
Spindled (sarcomatoid) mesothelioma occurs at both pleural and peritoneal sites; not restricted to a proper subset of the serosal-cavity ceiling.
Generic germ cell tumor descriptor arising across gonadal, mediastinal, CNS, retroperitoneal and other midline/extragonadal sites spanning the broad ceiling; not anatomically restricted.

Germinoma is the term for seminomatous-type germ cell tumors at extragonadal/CNS/mediastinal and gonadal sites, covering the broad ceiling of germ cell sites; not restricted to a proper subset by substantive evidence.
A histologic variant of germinoma occurring across the same broad germ cell tumor sites; not anatomically restricted.
Generic nonseminomatous germ cell tumor descriptor arising across gonadal, mediastinal, CNS, retroperitoneal and other extragonadal sites spanning the ceiling; not anatomically restricted.

A generic malignant teratoma descriptor; malignant teratomas arise across gonadal, mediastinal, CNS, sacrococcygeal, head/neck and other midline sites spanning the broad ceiling, and are not restricted to a proper subset.
Immature teratoma occurs across gonadal and multiple extragonadal midline sites (mediastinum, CNS, sacrococcygeal, head/neck); generic descriptor spanning the ceiling, not anatomically restricted.
Malignant immature teratoma occurs across gonadal and extragonadal midline sites; generic descriptor spanning the ceiling, not restricted to a proper subset.

Postpubertal-type teratoma is a category applied to gonadal (testis/ovary) and extragonadal germ cell sites; it is not confined to a single proper subset of the code's broad ceiling by substantive evidence.
A generic synonym for malignant teratoma occurring across gonadal and extragonadal midline sites; not anatomically restricted.
Generic malignant teratoma descriptor arising across gonadal, mediastinal, CNS, sacrococcygeal and other midline sites spanning the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
